prompt.context_jp: 「あの人って あんな不細工なのに 東大行って」
prompt.prompt_jp: あの人＿＿ あんな不細工なのに 東大行って
prompt.prompt_en: Nana is introducing a new characterization of Ryuji with surprise/contrast.

feedback.correct_en: Nana is making 'that person' the topic and commenting on him across multiple clauses — classic topic は. が would mark him as new, unexpected information in a single predication, which doesn't fit this ongoing commentary.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make him newly identified info; を is for direct objects and ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.en: As for that person, he's kind. (topic)
That person is the culprit. (identification/new info)

prompt.context_jp: 「あんな不細工でも 頑張れば 輝けるのだということを あの人は私に教えてくれました｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: あの人＿＿私に教えてくれました
prompt.prompt_en: Nana is talking about Ryuji as the known topic of her monologue.

feedback.correct_en: 'That person' is already the topic of her speech, so は is natural. が would spotlight him as newly identified, which doesn't match this reflective statement about an already-known subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce him as new information — but Nana has been talking about him all along.

contrast_examples.jp: あの人は教えてくれた。
contrast_examples.en: That person (whom we've been discussing) taught me.

contrast_examples.jp: あの人が教えてくれた。
contrast_examples.en: It was that person who taught me. (identifying who)

prompt.context_jp: 「あの人は 不細工という宿命に 逆らって 頑張ってるんです｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: あの人＿＿ 不細工という宿命に 逆らって 頑張ってるんです
prompt.prompt_en: Nana continues describing Ryuji as the ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: は keeps Ryuji as the running topic across Nana's extended description. が would re-foreground him as new/identificational, breaking the discourse flow.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would feel like introducing someone unknown — but we've been talking about him.

contrast_examples.en: He is the one working hard. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 「ひいきされてる者は 気が付かないんですよ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: ひいきされてる者＿＿ 気が付かないんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Ryuji is making a generic statement about a category of people.

feedback.correct_en: Generic/categorical statements ('people who are favored...') use は to set the category as topic. が would single out a specific individual, which clashes with the generalizing nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as 'it's favored people who don't notice' — overly exhaustive for a general observation.

prompt.context_jp: 「レンっていうプレーボーイ面した クソガキ＿＿いたんですよ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: レンっていうプレーボーイ面した クソガキ＿＿いたんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Ryuji is introducing a brand-new character into the story.

feedback.correct_en: Introducing a new character with 〜がいた is the textbook new-information が. は would presuppose the brat is already known.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require the listener to already know about Ren — but he's just being introduced.

contrast_examples.en: Long ago, there was a man. (introducing)

prompt.context_jp: 「そしたら 幼稚園の先生＿＿走って来て」
prompt.prompt_jp: 幼稚園の先生＿＿ 走って来て
prompt.prompt_en: A new participant suddenly enters the scene in Ryuji's story.

feedback.correct_en: The teacher is new information entering the narrative scene — が marks the arrival/appearance. は would wrongly presuppose she was already the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the teacher sound already-known or contrastive, which breaks the surprise of her arrival.

contrast_examples.en: The teacher came (as for the teacher...). (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「僕の父と母も不細工です｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕の父と母＿＿も不細工です → 僕＿＿ね 不細工の系譜を 僕の代で断ち切りたいんです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 僕 in sentence 0052.

feedback.correct_en: Ryuji sets himself up as the topic to make a personal declaration about his resolve. は is the natural self-topic marker in such statements of intent.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify 'it is I who want to end it,' sounding oddly combative here.

contrast_examples.en: I'll be the one to do it. (volunteering/exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 「万智が戻ってきてからというもの、営業所の主役は否応なく彼女ということになり…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 営業所の主役は否応なく彼女＿＿ということになり
prompt.prompt_en: The narration identifies exactly who the star of the office is.

feedback.correct_en: 'The star is her (and nobody else)' is exhaustive-listing が in a Y が X type identification. は would just topicalize her and lose the exclusive nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would read 'as for her, (she's) the star' — fine but weakens the 'it had to be her' exclusivity.

contrast_examples.jp: 犯人は彼だ／犯人が彼だ。

prompt.context_jp: 「店の扉が開き、新しい客が一人入ってきたのは、ちょうどそんな時だった。」
prompt.prompt_jp: 新しい客＿＿一人入ってきた
prompt.prompt_en: A new customer appears in the scene.

feedback.correct_en: A brand-new, unidentified customer entering uses event-reporting が. は would presuppose the customer is already known to the reader.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly treat 'the new customer' as an established topic.

prompt.context_jp: 「1人で飲みたい時もあるんだよ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 1人で飲みたい時＿＿あるんだよ
prompt.prompt_en: Adachi pushes back: there EXIST times when he wants to drink alone.

feedback.correct_en: も adds 'also/even such times exist', fitting the defensive nuance. が would just assert existence neutrally; は would contrast but less idiomatic here.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would sound like he's isolating 'alone-drinking times' from something else; が loses the 'even such times' flavor.

contrast_examples.en: There are even days like that.
There are days like that. (plain existence)

prompt.context_jp: 「その答えを聞いた足立の胸に、冷たいものがすっと落ちていった。」
prompt.prompt_jp: 足立の胸＿＿冷たいものがすっと落ちていった
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the destination/location where the cold feeling settles.

feedback.correct_en: 落ちる takes に for the endpoint of falling — the cold feeling lands IN his chest. で would mark a location of activity, not an endpoint.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks where an action takes place, not a landing point; を would mark a path, which is wrong here.

contrast_examples.en: I felt it in my chest. (locus of sensation)

prompt.context_jp: 「田部竜司の『がんばりノート』には、彼が人知れず積み重ねてきた日々が、几帳面な文字でびっしりと綴られている。」
prompt.prompt_jp: 田部竜司の『がんばりノート』＿＿は、彼＿＿人知れず積み重ねてきた日々が綴られている
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 彼 inside the relative clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside relative clauses, the subject is usually marked with が, not は. 彼が積み重ねてきた日々 'the days he has accumulated' is a subordinate clause subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は generally doesn't appear as the subject marker inside a relative/adnominal clause.

prompt.context_jp: 「私は課長の妻ですから 課長の元しか帰る所はないと 言ったはずです｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私＿＿課長の妻ですから
prompt.prompt_en: Machi explains her position by stating what she is.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for me, I am...' — a self-identifying declaration uses は. が would exhaustively identify 'I am the one who is your wife', which is pragmatically odd.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like answering 'who is your wife?' — not the context.

contrast_examples.en: I am the student (you asked about). (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 「給湯室で作りました｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 給湯室＿＿作りました
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking where she cooked.

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action takes place — she cooked AT the kitchenette. に would mark a destination or existence, not activity.
feedback.incorrect_en: に with 作る would wrongly imply 'into the kitchenette'; を is for direct objects.

prompt.context_jp: 「外見って重要な問題なんだよ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 外見＿＿重要な問題なんだよ (って ≒ ?)
prompt.prompt_en: Tabe makes a general claim about appearance as a topic.

feedback.correct_en: General statements about abstract concepts ('appearance is important') naturally take は as topic. って here is a colloquial topic marker ≈ は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively claim 'it's appearance that matters (not other things)' — a stronger, more contrastive meaning than Tabe's generalization.

prompt.context_jp: 「部屋全体が輝いて見える｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋全体＿＿輝いて見える
prompt.prompt_en: Tabe exclaims a spontaneous observation about the room.

feedback.correct_en: Spontaneous perceptual observations ('the whole room looks shiny!') use が — this is new, event-like information. は would make it sound like a measured, pre-planned remark.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize 'the room' as if introducing a known subject for comparison, losing the burst-of-surprise feel.

prompt.context_jp: 「偽りじゃ ない｡ その顔もまた 本当の奈々なんだ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: その顔もまた 本当の奈々＿＿んだ
prompt.prompt_en: Ryuji identifies that face as the real Nana.

feedback.correct_en: The copula な precedes んだ for noun predicates (本当の奈々なんだ). This isn't a particle slot for が/は; the identification is carried by the copula + explanatory のだ.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would ungrammatically split the noun phrase from んだ.

prompt.context_jp: 「クラスの人気者の マンチッチだった｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: クラスの＿＿のマンチッチだった
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the word describing Machi's status in the class.

feedback.correct_en: 人気者 'popular person' fits — young Machi is remembered as the beloved star of the class. 働き者 means 'hard worker' and 怠け者 means 'lazybones', neither matching.
feedback.incorrect_en: The context is social popularity, not work ethic or laziness.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼はクラスの人気者だ。

prompt.context_jp: 「これが いわゆる ギャップ萌えというものです！」
prompt.prompt_jp: これが＿＿ ギャップ萌えというものです
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the word meaning 'so-called'.

feedback.correct_en: いわゆる means 'so-called/what is known as' and attaches directly to a noun. いわば is 'so to speak' (used more adverbially); いまさら means 'at this late stage' — wrong meaning.
feedback.incorrect_en: いわば can precede a noun too but feels looser; いまさら doesn't fit at all here.

contrast_examples.en: They're like family, so to speak.

prompt.context_jp: 「僭越ながら 私が お2人の仲を修復します｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿＿ながら 私が お2人の仲を修復します
prompt.prompt_en: A humble preface before Machi's bold declaration.

feedback.correct_en: 僭越ながら is the set humble preface 'with all due respect/though it may be presumptuous of me'. 失礼ながら is close but softer ('excuse me, but'); 遠慮ながら isn't a standard phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: 失礼ながら works grammatically but is less fitting for taking bold action; 遠慮ながら is not a set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 僭越ながら申し上げます。
contrast_examples.en: With all due respect, I'll say...

prompt.context_jp: 「あんなブスに だまされてたと思うと ゾッとしますよ ゾッと｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: あんなブスに ＿＿てたと思うと ゾッとしますよ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb for 'been deceived/fooled'.

feedback.correct_en: だまされてた is the passive past-progressive 'had been deceived', matching Ryuji's self-pitying victim stance. だましてた would mean 'had been deceiving (someone)'.
feedback.incorrect_en: だましてた flips him into the deceiver; だませてた is potential past, not meaningful here.

prompt.context_jp: 「からかってんの？ いくら青山だからって このボロ家はないだろ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: この＿＿家はないだろ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the word describing the run-down house.

feedback.correct_en: ボロ家 means 'shabby, run-down house' — exactly Tabe's complaint about the exterior. ピカ (shiny) and モロ (fragile/directly) don't form this compound.
feedback.incorrect_en: ピカ家 isn't a word; モロ家 isn't either.

prompt.context_jp: 「汚いけど うまい店のほうが お気に入りの店となるのです｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 汚いけど うまい店の＿＿が お気に入りの店となるのです
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the comparative form.

feedback.correct_en: 〜のほうが X is the standard comparative 'the X one is more...'. そう and よう don't form comparatives.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のそうが and 〜のようが are ungrammatical.

prompt.context_jp: 「欲しいもの それは 家｡ 帰る家｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb modifying 'house' — 'a house to go home to'.

feedback.correct_en: 帰る 'to return home' modifies 家 in the deeply emotional phrase 'a house to go home to'. 返る means 'return (an object)' and 替わる means 'be replaced'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 返る is about objects returning; 替わる is substitution — both miss the 'go home' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: I have no place to return to.

prompt.context_jp: 「それと… 私 見ちゃったんです｡ 彼の『がんばりノート』｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私 見＿＿んです
prompt.prompt_en: Nana admits with slight guilt that she saw his notebook.

feedback.correct_en: 〜ちゃった (〜てしまった contracted) conveys the 'oops, I ended up doing it' nuance that fits Nana's confession. 見ました is neutral past; 見ている is ongoing, not a confession.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見ました lacks the regret/slip nuance; 見ているんです would mean 'I'm looking at it' now.

prompt.context_jp: Machi apologizes for visiting Nana's home as a formal first greeting.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as Machi's opening greeting in this polite visit?

choices.text: お宅までお邪魔して申し訳ございません。
あなたの家に来てごめんね。
家まで来ちゃってすまん。

feedback.correct_en: Machi's actual line uses お宅・お邪魔して・申し訳ございません — the stacked keigo appropriate for a first formal visit. The casual b/c would be jarring in this business-polite register.
feedback.incorrect_en: b is friendly-casual, c is masculine-blunt — both clash with Machi's formal realtor persona.

contrast_examples.jp: お邪魔して申し訳ございません。

prompt.context_jp: Yashiro asks Machi to show him her smile, and she responds.
prompt.prompt_en: Which reply best fits Machi's teasingly reluctant 'if you really insist' tone?

choices.text: どうしてもと おっしゃるなら。
絶対にって頼むんだったら。

feedback.correct_en: The actual line uses おっしゃる (keigo for 言う) matching Machi's unflappable polite register. b flattens the keigo; c is overly casual and verbose for her character.
feedback.incorrect_en: b loses the deferential nuance; c sounds like a different speaker entirely.

contrast_examples.jp: おっしゃるなら伺います。
contrast_examples.en: If you say so, I'll ask. (polite)
If you say so, I'll listen. (casual)

prompt.context_jp: Young employees gossiping in a casual bar.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line fits the casual youth-slang register of this scene?

choices.text: マジ やばたにえん。
誠に由々しき事態でございます。
本当に危険な状況だと思います。

feedback.correct_en: やばたにえん is slangy youth-speak ('super sketchy') that matches the casual bar banter. b is stiff keigo and c is textbook-neutral — both would feel out of place.
feedback.incorrect_en: b/c are polite/formal registers inappropriate for drunken peer gossip.

prompt.context_jp: Machi offers to show Tabe and Nana a house.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line is Machi's natural realtor-pitch wording?

choices.text: あなたと奈々様にピッタリの家をご案内します。
あなたと奈々様にピッタリの家を見せます。
あなたと奈々様にピッタリの家を教えます。

feedback.correct_en: ご案内する is the standard polite realtor/service verb for 'show you a property'. 見せる is bluntly 'show' and lacks the service-industry polish; 教える 'teach/inform' is wrong collocation with 家.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見せます is too casual for a sales context; 教えます would mean 'tell you about it', not escort you to view.

contrast_examples.en: I'll show you the property. (realtor polite)

prompt.context_jp: Rusudo confesses his lifelong feelings to Machi in the empty classroom.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line best fits the quiet, weighted confession of this scene?

choices.text: あの時と同じ気持ちで 僕は今もあなたを愛しています。
昔からお前が好きだわ。
今もあんたのことが好きかな。

feedback.correct_en: The actual line uses the measured, sincere 愛しています with 僕 and あなた — fitting a long-held, grown-up confession. b/c sound either too curt or too casual-flippant for this emotional climax.
feedback.incorrect_en: b's お前・好きだわ mix is tonally inconsistent; c's あんた・かな makes the confession sound uncertain and offhand.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたを愛しています。
